newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania ship docks in Italy, 1,000 believed aboard.
newsitem.headline: Albania ship docks in Italy, 1,000 believed aboard.

text.p: An Albanian refugee ship with up to 1,500 people on board limped into the southern Italian port of Bari on Sunday, one of two crowded ships racketeers attempted to send across the Adriatic.

"There are about 1,000 to 1,500 people on board," a coastguard official told Reuters by telephone. He said earlier estimates that the ship was carrying 700 refugees were made at night and perhaps did not take full account of those below deck.
Italian television showed the ageing tanker, the Irini, its pale blue paint eaten away with rust, filled to overflowing with Albanians, who were even climbing up two masts on deck.

"I believe this episode will be one of the last and I hope we can all keep our cool so as not to turn what is unfortunately a fact of life into an emergency," Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told reporters in Italy's Adriatic resort of Rimini.
Some 13,000 Albanians fled to Italy in March on decrepit boats to escape a wave of violence sparked by the collapse of high-risk savings funds that swept their nation towards anarchy.

Coastguards intercepted the ship when it left Albanian waters on Saturday evening and tried in vain to persuade it to turn back. Several coastguard, police and navy vessels escorted it to Bari for disembarking expected to take up to three hours.
Officials said the ship was carrying many women and children and two heavily pregnant women were escorted to military buses. Some 60 volunteers lined the quayside to help the operation.
Smugglers slipped the Irini past Italian navy vessels and set sail from Velipoje Beach, 30 km (20 miles) south of Shkoder in northern Albania on Saturday.
Another Italian coastguard spokesman said there were unconfirmed reports that a second ship packed with refugees also left from near Velipoje but was stationary in Albanian waters.
Security sources in Tirana said the Irini had been bought in Montenegro for $120,000 by a gang based in northern Albania that is organising the lucrative traffic of illegal immigrants.
Albanians desperate to flee the impoverished Balkan nation pay about $500 each for a place on a boat.

Coastguard officials said they had plucked one Albanian from the sea when the ship was some 12 miles offshore, but could not immediately confirm a television report quoting the man as saying he had been thrown overboard by an armed, masked man.

The Italian command said troops from a 6,000-strong multinational force sent to secure Albania's ports and roads and to protect humanitarian aid deliveries were not yet deployed in the north to prevent departures of this kind.

"At Vlore (in the south), traffic of illegal immigrants is no longer active with troops securing the port. Maybe the traffic from the north could stop when the multinational force is deployed there in the next two weeks," spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Giovanni Bernardi told Reuters in Tirana.
Last Sunday, Italian authorities at Barletta rescued 571 Albanians packed into an ageing vessel built for 50 that had left from Velipoje, taking 26 hours to reach Italy.
The conditions in which Albanians are transported are appalling and there have been tragic consequences.
An estimated 103 people drowned on March 28 when an overcrowded ship from Vlore collided with an Italian navy frigate 30 miles off Brindisi and sank.
The current crisis in Albania exploded when protesters angered over the loss of savings took to the streets, blaming President Sali Berisha for not taking action against the funds.
As law and order collapsed, Albanians raided military arsenals, taking up arms for self-protection or for criminal purposes. An estimated 700 people have died since February.
